newsitem.title: CANADA: OLYMPICS-MARC CRAWFORD NAMED COACH OF CANADA OLYMPICS TEAM.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-MARC CRAWFORD NAMED COACH OF CANADA OLYMPICS TEAM.

text.p: Colorado Avalanche head coach Marc Crawford, who guided the team to a Stanley Cup in 1996, was named head coach of the 1998 Canadian Olympic ice hockey team Monday.

"I'm very appreciative of the opportunity to represent my country, our country, with the other great Olympic athletes that will be in Nagano, and the other great Olympic coaches that will be there as well," said Crawford. "We look forward to the challenge of the Nagano Olympics."

New Philadelphia Flyers head coach Wayne Cashman, Andy Murray and Mike Johnson were named to round out the coaching staff. Cashman was named head coach of the Flyers last month. Murray is the coach of the Calgary-based national team and Johnson is his associate coach.
Crawford, 36, helped Colorado to the 1997 President's Cup for the best record in the NHL. He was awarded the 1995 Jack Adams Trophy as the NHL Coach of the Year.

Crawford and his staff were picked by Bob Clarke of the Flyers and his assistants, Bob Gainey of the Dallas Stars and Pierre Gauthier of the Ottawa Senators. All three are the general managers of their NHL clubs.
Clarke also addressed the possibility of Team Canada enlisting the help of centre Mario Lemieux, who retired at the end of this season from the Pittsburgh Penguins.

"When I spoke with Mario, he was very non-committal," said Clarke. "I would say that we would call him and find out if he is willing to put in the training time and play some games to get himself ready. I would think it's highly doubtful, though."
Crawford's father was the captain of the Canadian team that won the 1959 World Championships in Prague, Czechoslovakia.

There is heavy pressure on Team Canada's entry to bring home the gold medal in the 1998 Winter Olympics at Nagno, Japan, after the United States won last summer's inaugural World Cup of Hockey, taking the final two games in Montreal.
That defeat is widely believed to have cost Edmonton Oilers president and general manager Glen Sather his post as Team Canada GM.
The chance for redemption comes during a 16-day shutdown in the middle of the 1997-98 NHL season.
